questions.q: The visual pigment in rods is:
questions.exp: The page identifies rhodopsin as the visual pigment. (Book p229)

questions.q: Match rhodopsin's components with their roles — 1) Opsin/scotopsin  2) 11-cis retinal … A) Light-sensitive chromophore  B) GPCR that enables signalling
questions.exp: Opsin/scotopsin is a GPCR enabling signalling; 11-cis retinal is the light-sensitive chromophore. (Book p229)

questions.q: After absorbing light, 11-cis retinal isomerizes to the more stable ___ retinal.
questions.exp: Light absorption converts 11-cis retinal to the more stable 11-trans retinal isomer. (Book p229)

questions.q: The visual cycle shown occurs in rod photoreceptors; RBP transports retinol in blood and IRBP means:
questions.exp: The site is rod photoreceptors; RBP is retinol-binding protein and IRBP is intraretinal binding protein. (Book p229)

questions.q: Which sequence best describes retinoid recycling in the visual cycle?
opts: All-trans retinal forms rhodopsin directly; light converts it to vitamin D
11-cis retinal is irreversibly degraded and replaced by melanin
11-cis retinoid forms rhodopsin; light produces all-trans retinal, which is recycled via retinol/retinyl esters to 11-cis retinal
Opsin converts retinyl esters directly into cGMP
questions.exp: Vitamin-A-derived retinoids are carried by RBP/IRBP; all-trans retinal is recycled through retinol and retinyl esters, with RPE-linked regeneration of 11-cis retinoid. (Book p229)

questions.q: A mutation in the RPE-65 gene disrupts visual-pigment regeneration. The chromophore that cannot be regenerated is:
questions.exp: RPE-65-dependent regeneration produces 11-cis retinal, which recombines with opsin to form rhodopsin. (Book p229)

questions.q: The unstable light-activated intermediate that acts as an enzyme in phototransduction for milliseconds is:
questions.exp: Metarhodopsin II is an unstable intermediate, acts within milliseconds and functions as an enzyme for phototransduction. (Book p229)

opts: Metarhodopsin II → transducin (GDP-GTP exchange) → PDE activation
questions.exp: Metarhodopsin II activates transducin by GDP-to-GTP exchange; transducin activates phosphodiesterase. (Book p230)
Activated PDE hydrolyses cGMP to 5-prime GMP. (Book p230)

questions.q: When cGMP concentration falls, which photoreceptor changes occur?
opts: Na+ channels open, Na+ influx rises and glutamate release rises
Ca2+ channels open and action potentials begin in rods
Na+ channels close, Na+ influx stops and glutamate efflux stops
Chloride channels close while glutamate efflux increases
questions.exp: Reduced cGMP closes Na+ channels, stopping Na+ influx and glutamate efflux. (Book p230)

questions.q: The light response in a photoreceptor is a graded hyperpolarising local potential, not an action potential.
opts: It is an all-or-none rod action potential
It is a graded depolarising potential
questions.exp: Photoreceptor hyperpolarisation is graded, is not an action potential and is transmitted by electronic conduction. (Book p230)

questions.q: The phototransduction signal passes first to bipolar cells and then to ganglion cells, where:
questions.exp: The signal reaches bipolar cells, then ganglion cells; ganglion cells are the site of action potentials. (Book p230)

questions.q: The visual pathway reaches the lateral geniculate body, which has ___ layers.
questions.exp: The LGB is shown with six layers. (Book p230)

questions.q: Match LGB layers and pathway — 1) Layers 1-2  2) Layers 3-6 … A) Parvocellular: fine details and colour  B) Magnocellular: motion and black-and-white
questions.exp: LGB layers 1-2 are magnocellular for motion/black-and-white; layers 3-6 are parvocellular for fine detail/colour. (Book p230)

questions.q: A photoreceptor exposed to light becomes hyperpolarised; in darkness it is:
opts: At resting potential with an action potential
Unable to release neurotransmitter under either condition
questions.exp: The page contrasts hyperpolarisation under light with a depolarising state under dark. (Book p230)

questions.q: RPE-65 mutation prevents regeneration of 11-cis retinal and is linked to:
opts: Retinitis pigmentosa and Leber congenital amaurosis
questions.exp: The diagram links RPE-65 gene mutation and lack of 11-cis retinal regeneration with retinitis pigmentosa and Leber congenital amaurosis. (Book p230)

units.title: Rhodopsin and visual cycle
units.guide: Rhodopsin consists of opsin (a GPCR) and 11-cis retinal chromophore. Light isomerizes retinal; the rod visual cycle recycles vitamin-A-derived retinoids across photoreceptor and RPE, with RPE-65 required for regeneration.

units.title: Phototransduction cascade
units.guide: Metarhodopsin II activates transducin and PDE, reducing cGMP. Na+ channels close, glutamate release stops and the photoreceptor hyperpolarises; graded signals reach bipolar cells and then ganglion-cell action potentials.

units.title: Lateral geniculate pathways and light/dark response
units.guide: The ganglion-cell visual signal reaches the six-layer LGB. Layers 1-2 are magnocellular (motion, black-and-white); layers 3-6 are parvocellular (fine detail, colour). Light hyperpolarises photoreceptors; darkness depolarises them.
